questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me personally, it was important to do exchange in an English speaking country because I study English, and I visited Dublin a couple years ago and just fell in love with it, so that's why I chose Dublin.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. I was still difficult to figure it all out because there was so much information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, other than a short lecture during the intro week

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I don't think it was offered directly to us, you kind of had to seek it out. We did get some crucial information via email of course, but not everything

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Apartments mostly, either shared or own room, and the same with toilets

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a fully functioning kitchen and a store on campus, though it didn't have the best selection for a good fulling healthy meal

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it's important to not just be on campus most of the time. You have to actively seek other stuff because it's easy to get comfortable in safe surroundings

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to check in once you knew where to go

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You gave your information, like name and student number, and then they checked you in and showed you to your room

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The students that are working at the student desk

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful — I also ended up switching courses which wasn't that difficult either

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it, there is help to find

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly easy classes, since I didn't want to spend all my time there with my nose in a book. But even though I did take mostly entry level courses, they were still very good and different to what I was used to in my host university

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit more hand-held at some points, and there were also a lot more midterms and other assessments during the semester

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Children's Literature, Exploring Ireland, Dark Romanticism, Multilingualism, and Literature and Crisis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Children's Literature is a very good course where we work with children's book, obviously. The professor was very sweet and really enthusiastic, and that really provided a good environment in the course. It was also nice to read some book from my own childhood and read some of those I haven't gotten a chance to read yet

Dark Romanticism is also a very interesting course, though it is very different to Children's Literature. We dealt with darker themes and read books which aren't on the regular curriculum usually. But if you're interested in the gothic or dealing with themes such as moral corruption, drug addiction, monstrosity, this course could be something for you. Also, the professor is lovely.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than expected. Accommodation was also very expensive, but they do have a housing crisis in Dublin

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really do many clubs or societies, but there were many to choose from, if you want to engage in that

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were really a lot of clubs, like close to a hundred clubs with anything you can imagine

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to pubs, which is very cultural is Dublin

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: St. Patrick's Day is a great experience, but also go out and see and experience all there is. Also take opportunities to go see other stuff in other cities, take day trips or weekend trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded because they're were outgoing and they love to drink pints

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, other than adjusting to being more outgoing as well

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The drinking culture, I felt just at home

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minden and be outgoing. It could be quite lonely is you find yourself with no social life during your exchange because your so far away from home. 
Give yourself grace. You can't do it all, so even though I would encourage going out with your friends and having fun, you also have to pace yourself. Take breaks if you need them.
Don't neglect your studies. Maybe getting the best grades isn't the biggest priority, but it's still important to keep up with your assignments and readings, and it's still interesting stuff you learn. You can be both studious and social during your exchange

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's good to keep track of what you need to do regarding stuff like what's on Mobility Online, and when you need to sign stuff or show up to stuff. Don't get completely lost in the excitement of it all – and read your emails!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and experiencing of a new and exciting culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my apartment at home. I felt a bit homesick throughout my exchange, but I'm still very happy that I decided to do it though!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
